title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Data Visualization Design
text:
This first chapter emphasizes with concrete examples the importance of data visualization for understanding the world, communicating with other people and having impact in the world.
The goal of this chapter is to enforce the idea that it is important to not just “show the data” and that instead designing effective data visualization is purposeful and requires particular skills and knowledge.

title: Syllabus
text:
This course provides a hands-on introduction to designing effective data visualizations.





Will cover examples illustrating the importance of designing effective data visualizations.
Students will be asked to pick 3 good and 3 bad examples from their fields and comment them (why they like or dislike them; at the end of the course they will redo that and maybe redesign one of them in Figma).



I will present my 10 principles for good data visualization; we will review some graphs and critisize them together; based on work they’ve done in 1.



There are many tools for creating data visualization; we will use Figma to learn about how to draft a data visualization.



Picking the right type of graph for your data; know your data viz vocabulary



Tools; Testing you data visualization;



Presenting some tools/software for making graphs (e.g., ggplot2, D3); Cover other forms of visualization (e.g., dashboards, diagrams, visual explanations, infographics)



Students are organized in groups and asked to work on particular data visualization projects.

title: Data Visualization Design
text:
Of the 13 charts circulated by Thiokol managers and engineers to the scattered teleconferees,


six contained no tabled data about either O-ring temperature, O-ring blow-by, or O-ring anomaly (these were primarily outlines of arguments being made by the Thiokol engineers).


Of the seven remaining charts containing data,


six of them included data on either launch temperatures or O-ring anomaly but not both in relation to each other.


Only one chart relating O-ring temperature and O-ring damage was prepared by a Thiokol engineer.





Let’s focus on this one document.

Anscombe’s Quartet

Constructed in 1973 by statistician Francis Anscombe
Demonstrates the importance of graphing data
Shows the effect of outliers on statistical properties
Intended to counter the impression among statisticians that “numerical calculations are exact, but graphs are rough.”

section: The two purposes of data visualization
text:
The two purposes of data visualization

The key function of data visualization is to move information from point A to point B.



In exploratory visualization,


  


point A is the dataset andpoint B is the designer’s own mind.




In explanatory visualization,


  


point A is the mind of the designer, andpoint B is the mind of the reader.”





Julie Steele & Noah Iliinsky, Designing Data Visualizations
